chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Rector's Club and pooling pay for Dad Cook
summary: Bechet and Peyton doubled with Mitchell's Rector's Club and made good money, while Briggs and others pooled pay to cover Cook's expenses without his knowing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And when we finished at the Palais de Hammersmith, Bechet and Benny Peyton's bunch, they continued and they doubled, then doubled with the Rector's Club which was owned by Mr. Mitchell, they played two jobs.
They had afternoons from 3:00 to 6:00 and 9:00 to 12:00. Then they worked for this extra crowd at the Rector's Club, from say the cocktail hour about 3:00 or 3:30.
They made plenty money. They made plenty of money.

So, Dad Cook himself, he didn't have to worry about anything, because we had a feeling, when we worked, Dad Cook, when our bunch folded, Dad was still in London, you see. He didn't have to worry about anything, 'cause we all pooled, automatically, he didn't know.
But we pooled the pay, all his expenses and everything else. He didn't have to worry about anything. He didn't appreciate it, because he was very independent, you see.
But the spirit was there, and we did nicely.
